# Kspec Automation Session - Task Work

**Session ID:** `01KJN28PAZMZDSX3RKS2M01JZJ`
**Iteration:** 1 of 30
**Mode:** Automated (no human in the loop)


### Current State

> **Truncated** (103588 bytes). Fetch full data:
> ```
> kspec session start --json
> ```
>
> Summary: `{}`

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

Shadow Branch Auto-Commit
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KFMFAQ94G3162ZKGB2N02K3W
Slugs:     trait-shadow-commit
Type:      trait

─── Description ───
Commands that modify shadow branch state automatically commit changes with semantic messages

─── Acceptance Criteria ───
  [ac-1]
    Given: command modifies state in shadow worktree
    When: save operation completes successfully
    Then: git commit is created in shadow branch with semantic message
  [ac-2]
    Given: shadow commit is created
    When: commit message is generated
    Then: message follows pattern operation-colon-ref-short with optional detail
  [ac-3]
    Given: shadow commit is created
    When: item reference is available
    Then: commit message includes ULID prefix (8 chars) or primary slug
  [ac-4]
    Given: shadow is not configured (no worktree)
    When: command that would normally commit runs
    Then: command completes successfully without attempting git operations
  [ac-5]
    Given: save operation fails
    When: validation or IO error occurs
    Then: no commit is attempted and error is returned
  [ac-6]
    Given: shadow has remote configured
    When: commit succeeds
    Then: push is attempted in fire-and-forget mode (failure doesn't block command)
  [ac-7]
    Given: commit or push fails
    When: save succeeded but git operation failed
    Then: command succeeds but outputs warning about sync state
  [ac-8]
    Given: command performs multiple related saves
    When: all saves complete successfully
    Then: single atomic commit covers all changes

gh pr create --title "fix(skill): commit render hashes to shadow branch after skill render" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

- **Bug**: `kspec skill render` wrote `.render-hash-<platform>` files to the `.kspec/` shadow worktree but did not call `commitIfShadow`, leaving uncommitted changes that required a manual `git commit/push` on `kspec-meta`
- **Fix**: Added `commitIfShadow` call in the render action (in `skill-diff.ts`) after all rendering and cleanup completes — creates a single atomic commit covering all rendered skills (AC: @trait-shadow-commit ac-8)
- **Regression tests**: New `tests/shadow-skill-commit.test.ts` with 6 tests verifying all mutating skill commands (add, import, set, render single, render all, delete) leave the shadow branch clean after execution

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run tests/shadow-skill-commit.test.ts` — all 6 regression tests pass (2 were failing before fix)
- [x] `npm run test:shard1` — 1241 passed, no regressions
- [x] `npm run test:shard2` — 1371 passed, 1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this change
- [x] `npm run test:shard3` — 1012 passed, 1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this change
- [x] `npx vitest run tests/skill-cli.test.ts tests/skill-rendering.test.ts tests/skill-diff.test.ts tests/skill-meta-integration.test.ts` — 191 passed
- [x] `kspec validate` — Skills: OK

## Root cause

The concrete regression was observed in PR prep: after `skill import/set/render`, `.kspec` had pending changes (`skills/*/SKILL.md` + `.render-hash*` files) and required manual commit/push (kspec-meta commit `bcda69ab`).

All other skill commands (`skill add`, `import`, `set`, `delete`) already called `commitIfShadow` correctly. Only `skill render` was missing the call.

Task: @01KJF06N
Spec: @trait-shadow-commit

Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)
EOF
)"

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

Spec ref:  @ralph-subagent-spawning
Tags:      cli, ralph

─── Spec Context ───
Ralph Subagent Spawning
Type: requirement
Implementation: implemented
Description:
  Ralph can spawn ACP subagents for dedicated tasks (e.g., PR review). Subagents are separate Claude Code processes with focused prompts. Subagents run sequentially (ralph waits for completion).
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: ralph needs subagent
    When: spawn initiated
    Then: new ACP process started with dedicated prompt
  [ac-2]
    Given: subagent spawned
    When: prompt provided
    Then: prompt includes task ref, skill to invoke (/pr-review @task), context, and explicit review-only role boundary (never fix code)
  [ac-3]
    Given: subagent running
    When: ralph behavior
    Then: ralph waits for subagent completion before continuing
  [ac-4]
    Given: subagent runs
    When: display
    Then: subagent output rendered same as main agent (single stream)
  [ac-5]
    Given: subagent completes
    When: signaling
    Then: task status change (completed/needs_review) indicates outcome
  [ac-6]
    Given: multiple pending_review tasks
    When: spawning
    Then: processes one at a time sequentially
  [ac-7]
    Given: subagent runs
    When: resource management
    Then: respects ralph's --max-retries and failure limits
  [ac-8]
    Given: ralph iteration begins
    When: ralph checks task statuses
    Then: pending_review tasks detected trigger subagent spawn by ralph (host) before main agent iteration continues
  [ac-9]
    Given: subagent is running
    When: subagent exceeds timeout (default 10 minutes)
    Then: ralph terminates subagent and marks task automation: needs_review with timeout note
  [ac-10]
    Given: subagent prompt is built

  [ac-12]

Multi-Value Status Filter
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KHA83NGHKRZ287PGZ8HH6N0X
Slugs:     multi-value-status-filter
Type:      requirement
Maturity:  draft
Implementation: implemented

─── Description ───
The --status filter on list commands should accept multiple values via
comma-separated syntax or repeated flags. The backend ItemIndex.query()
already supports TaskStatus[] -- this closes the gap in the CLI layer.
Agents currently pipe through grep to filter by multiple statuses.
tasks list uses TaskStatus values (pending, in_progress, pending_review,
blocked, completed, cancelled) while item list uses ImplementationStatus
values (not_started, in_progress, implemented, verified). Validation must
use the correct enum per command.


─── Acceptance Criteria ───
  [ac-comma-separated]
    Given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress,pending_review
    When: A comma-separated status value is provided
    Then: Tasks matching ANY of the listed statuses are returned
  [ac-repeated-flag]
    Given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress --status pending_review
    When: The --status flag is provided multiple times
    Then: Tasks matching ANY of the listed statuses are returned (same as comma-separated)
  [ac-single-value-unchanged]
    Given: User runs kspec tasks list --status pending
    When: A single status value is provided
    Then: Behavior is unchanged from current -- only tasks with that status are returned
  [ac-invalid-task-status]
    Given: User runs kspec tasks list --status invalid_value
    When: An invalid TaskStatus name is provided
    Then: Error message lists valid TaskStatus values and exits non-zero
  [ac-invalid-item-status]
    Given: User runs kspec item list --status invalid_value
    When: An invalid ImplementationStatus name is provided
    Then: Error message lists valid ImplementationStatus values and exits non-zero
  [ac-item-list-parity]
    Given: User runs kspec item list --status implemented,verified
    When: Multi-value status is used on item list with ImplementationStatus values
    Then: Same comma-separated and repeated-flag behavior works for spec item listing
  [ac-json-output]
    Given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress,pending --json
    When: Combined with --json flag
    Then: JSON output contains only tasks matching the specified statuses
  [ac-trailing-comma]
    Given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress, (trailing comma)
    When: A trailing or leading comma produces an empty string after split
    Then: Empty strings are silently ignored, only valid status values are used

─── Inherited from @trait-filterable-list ───
  [ac-1] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: list command supports filtering
    When: --status <value> provided
    Then: only items with matching status shown
  [ac-2] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: list command supports filtering
    When: --tag <value> provided
    Then: only items with matching tag shown
  [ac-3] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: list command supports pagination
    When: --limit N provided
    Then: output shows at most N items
  [ac-4] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: list command supports pagination
    When: --offset N provided
    Then: output skips first N items
  [ac-5] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: multiple filters provided
    When: --status X --tag Y used together
    Then: output shows items matching all filters (AND logic)
  [ac-6] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: no items match filters
    When: list command executes
    Then: empty list shown with informative message
  [ac-7] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: list command output
    When: results are displayed
    Then: summary shows total matching items and filter state
  [ac-8] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: list command supports count mode
    When: --count flag is provided
    Then: outputs only the total number of matching items as a plain integer (no item details); ignores --limit and --offset; in JSON mode outputs {"count": N}

─── Inherited from @trait-json-output ───
  [ac-1] (from @trait-json-output)
    Given: command supports JSON mode
    When: --json flag is provided
    Then: output is valid JSON with no ANSI color codes
  [ac-2] (from @trait-json-output)
    Given: JSON mode is active
    When: command completes successfully
    Then: output includes all data available in human-readable mode

    Given: JSON mode is active

    Then: error is returned as JSON object with error field

    Given: JSON output contains references
    When: output is generated
    Then: references use @ prefix consistently
  [ac-5] (from @trait-json-output)
    Given: JSON output contains timestamps
    When: output is generated
    Then: timestamps use ISO 8601 format
  [ac-6] (from @trait-json-output)
    Given: command supports --json
    When: used with other formatting flags
    Then: --json takes precedence over other format options

The --status filter on list commands should accept multiple values via
comma-separated syntax or repeated flags. The backend ItemIndex.query()
already supports TaskStatus[] -- this closes the gap in the CLI layer.
Agents currently pipe through grep to filter by multiple statuses.
tasks list uses TaskStatus values (pending, in_progress, pending_review,
blocked, completed, cancelled) while item list uses ImplementationStatus
values (not_started, in_progress, implemented, verified). Validation must
use the correct enum per command.


─── Acceptance Criteria ───
  [ac-comma-separated]
    Given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress,pending_review
    When: A comma-separated status value is provided
    Then: Tasks matching ANY of the listed statuses are returned
  [ac-repeated-flag]
    Given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress --status pending_review
    When: The --status flag is provided multiple times
    Then: Tasks matching ANY of the listed statuses are returned (same as comma-separated)
  [ac-single-value-unchanged]
    Given: User runs kspec tasks list --status pending
    When: A single status value is provided
    Then: Behavior is unchanged from current -- only tasks with that status are returned
  [ac-invalid-task-status]
    Given: User runs kspec tasks list --status invalid_value
    When: An invalid TaskStatus name is provided
    Then: Error message lists valid TaskStatus values and exits non-zero
  [ac-invalid-item-status]
    Given: User runs kspec item list --status invalid_value
    When: An invalid ImplementationStatus name is provided
    Then: Error message lists valid ImplementationStatus values and exits non-zero
  [ac-item-list-parity]
    Given: User runs kspec item list --status implemented,verified
    When: Multi-value status is used on item list with ImplementationStatus values
    Then: Same comma-separated and repeated-flag behavior works for spec item listing
  [ac-json-output]
    Given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress,pending --json
    When: Combined with --json flag
    Then: JSON output contains only tasks matching the specified statuses
  [ac-trailing-comma]
    Given: User runs kspec tasks list --status in_progress, (trailing comma)
    When: A trailing or leading comma produces an empty string after split
    Then: Empty strings are silently ignored, only valid status values are used

─── Inherited from @trait-filterable-list ───
  [ac-1] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: list command supports filtering
    When: --status <value> provided
    Then: only items with matching status shown
  [ac-2] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: list command supports filtering
    When: --tag <value> provided
    Then: only items with matching tag shown
  [ac-3] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: list command supports pagination
    When: --limit N provided
    Then: output shows at most N items
  [ac-4] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: list command supports pagination
    When: --offset N provided
    Then: output skips first N items
  [ac-5] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: multiple filters provided
    When: --status X --tag Y used together
    Then: output shows items matching all filters (AND logic)
  [ac-6] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: no items match filters
    When: list command executes
    Then: empty list shown with informative message
  [ac-7] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: list command output
    When: results are displayed
    Then: summary shows total matching items and filter state
  [ac-8] (from @trait-filterable-list)
    Given: list command supports count mode
    When: --count flag is provided
    Then: outputs only the total number of matching items as a plain integer (no item details); ignores --limit and --offset; in JSON mode outputs {"count": N}

─── Inherited from @trait-json-output ───
  [ac-1] (from @trait-json-output)

  [ac-2] (from @trait-json-output)

  [ac-3] (from @trait-json-output)

  started_at: DateTimeSchema,
  paused_at?: DateTimeSchema,
  completed_at?: DateTimeSchema,
  step_results: StepResultSchema[],

}
```

```typescript
{
  step_index: number,
  status: 'completed' | 'skipped' | 'failed',

  notes?: string,

}
```

}

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.
